subject: Climate & Environment
title: Open Dumping in the Developing World
description: Learn Open Dumping in the Developing World in one minute.

hook.text: Over 2 billion people worldwide have no access to formal waste collection at all.

buildup.text: In many countries, waste is burned in open pits or dumped in rivers and fields.

discovery.text: Open dumps leach toxins into drinking water and breed disease-carrying mosquitoes and rats.

twist.text: Waste pickers sort these dumps by hand — earning survival wages while facing severe health risks.

climax.text: Formalizing waste picking and building basic infrastructure could transform waste management.

punchline.text: The waste crisis is a poverty crisis wearing a different name.

quiz.question: How many people lack access to formal waste collection?

details.summary: About 40 percent of the world's waste is disposed of in open dumps, with no liners, leachate collection, or gas capture. These sites contaminate groundwater, poison surrounding communities, and release uncontrolled methane.
details.whyItMatters: Open dumps are the worst form of waste disposal, posing severe health and environmental risks. Closing them and transitioning to managed systems is critical for global waste management.
takeaways: About 40 percent of global waste goes to open dumps
No environmental controls protect surrounding communities
Dump fires release toxic smoke and carcinogens

faq.question: How do open dumps affect nearby communities?
faq.answer: Residents suffer from toxic smoke when waste burns, contaminated water from leaching chemicals, disease spread by scavenging animals and insects, and respiratory illness from airborne pollutants. Those living closest, often the poorest, bear the heaviest health burden.

faq.question: What does it cost to close an open dump?
faq.answer: Costs vary enormously, but transitioning from open dumping to sanitary landfill or alternative systems requires investment in site remediation, new collection infrastructure, and ongoing operational funding. International financing and technical assistance are often essential.
